records.text: Arthas is presented as Prince of Lordaeron during Stratholme’s purge. He dismisses Uther and the paladins, then orders the infected people killed rather than let them become Mal’Ganis’s undead slaves. He divides his forces between fighting the Scourge and purging the city, urging those willing to save the land to follow him. His words show command and grim resolve.

Chromie guides adventurers through Stratholme's past, warning that the Infinite Dragonflight seeks to deceive Arthas and alter his fateful decision. She also raises the alarm that a colleague, a Guardian of Time, has been captured, and urges a rescue while keeping Arthas the priority.
An undead Enraging Ghoul of Stratholme, a dangerous common creature rather than a named individual.
An Acolyte, a humanoid attendant in Stratholme who strikes with shadow magic, Shadow Shock.
An undead Crypt Fiend of Stratholme, a common foe rather than a named individual.
A Patchwork Construct, an undead assembled creature of Stratholme.
An undead risen zombie, one of many in the Culling of Stratholme.
A Lordaeron Footman, a humanoid soldier of Stratholme who braces behind a Defend stance in battle.
A humanoid Lordaeron knight in the Culling of Stratholme.
A humanoid High Elf mage-priest in the Culling of Stratholme.
A humanoid High Elf sorceress in the Culling of Stratholme.

Silvio Perelli is a traveling salesman whose merchandise draws Sergeant Morigan’s scrutiny during an investigation of tampered food. When Morigan finds suspicious grain and moves to confiscate it, Silvio protests that he is innocent and challenges the sergeant’s accusation, though other recorded replies address Morigan respectfully.

Sergeant Morigan investigates signs of tampering in Silvio Perelli’s goods, discovers suspicious grain, and says it will be confiscated while Prince Arthas checks it. Morigan tells Silvio to report Scourge activity or shady dealings and asks what he has heard in his travels, showing both concern about the threat and use of the merchant as a source of information.
Martha Goslin welcomes Jena Anderson and readily lets her borrow grain when Jena says she has run out of flour for bread. Their exchange shows Martha helping a neighbor with household food supplies.

Jena Anderson is planning healthy meals for a man still recovering from an illness. As she weighs what food he has already eaten, she asks Martha Goslin for grain to make bread after running out of flour, then thanks her and says she owes her one.

Roger Owens is working with grain and looks forward to refreshments and conversation at an inn. When he notices the grain smells wrong, he decides to find a guard; his self-deprecating joke about needing a bath gives way to concern.

Bartleby Battson is a grain carrier whose cart has broken and horse lost a shoe, leaving his cargo to spoil and his schedule at risk. Frustrated by the shipment’s trouble, he darkly expects officials may blame plague and say everyone will die.
Nell is a beast in The Culling of Stratholme.
Pepper is a beast in The Culling of Stratholme.
A public crier of Lordaeron.

Chromie works to protect the timeline from the Infinite Dragonflight, whose deception could keep Arthas from making his fateful decision at Stratholme. She sends adventurers to expose the plagued grain and to stand by Arthas, watches for another foreign presence, and warns that the Guardian of Time is fading.
A Stratholme citizen who calls on Prince Arthas for help as townspeople fall seriously ill. The citizen's brief later reaction conveys shock at the unfolding crisis.
A Stratholme resident whose brief reaction, “Oh, no...,” conveys alarm during the culling sequence.
A Bile Golem, an undead construct of Stratholme that casts spells in battle.
A Devouring Ghoul, an undead creature of Stratholme.
Postmaster Malown is the postmaster in the Culling of Stratholme.
Hearthsinger Forresten is a humanoid who voices skepticism about the situation and expresses relief with a prayer of thanks to the Light.
Fras Siabi is a humanoid who questions a strange order involving suspicious food and jokes that Belfast should be arrested under the same standard.

Footman James treats the Prince’s commands as binding, remarking that orders are orders. He also reassures people concerned about befouled grain, recalling that his shift ended without finding any there. His account stays within what he personally observed, offering a limited report rather than claiming the wider problem is resolved.
Footman Maxwell is a humanoid footman in The Culling of Stratholme.
Carlin Redpath is a humanoid in The Culling of Stratholme.
Marlene Redpath is a humanoid in The Culling of Stratholme.
Pamela Redpath is a humanoid in The Culling of Stratholme.

Gryan Stoutmantle tells Mal that the soldiers’ work matters because the people’s safety comes first. He urges Mal to weigh that danger against the customers who need to live long enough to spend another day. The exchange shows Gryan defending the soldiers’ work and putting public safety ahead of business concerns.
Joseph Redpath is a humanoid in The Culling of Stratholme.

Emery Neill is the Stone Crow's barkeep, and says it is closed amid a health scare. He worries that Ed will be blamed for making people sick, and points to the orphanage children's evacuation as another reason to keep the tavern shut. His words show a cautious response to the danger.

Michael Belfast is a cook who guards the food in his cellar during a food scare. He angrily sends strangers away from it, and warns that he will stop serving ale when he overhears someone. His sharp reactions show how seriously he takes the disturbance and the protection of his goods.
Duke is a beast in The Culling of Stratholme.
Arion is a beast in The Culling of Stratholme.

Magistrate Barthilas is a worried civic figure in plague-stricken Stratholme. He fears that illness, ineffective remedies, and rumors about poisoned food will turn neighbors against one another and plunge the city into bedlam. Feeling ill himself, he wonders whether stress is causing ulcers and feels powerless to help.

Chromie is associated with the Bronze Dragonflight and works to protect the historical course of the Culling of Stratholme. She warns that the Infinite Dragonflight may still interfere and asks for help accompanying Arthas through the event and against Mal'Ganis. Her words describe the episode as a consequential thread of history.

Mal Corricks is a barkeeper in Stratholme. During the epidemic scare, he tells Michael that business is suffering and the tavern needs every copper. He grudgingly nods before conceding that he cannot argue, showing his concern with keeping the business afloat amid the city's crisis.
Edward Orrick is a cook.
Stephanie Sindree sells fruit and fish. When confronted about her food, she protests that it was not hers and offers a refund, clearly caught up in a dispute and worried about the consequences.
Olivia Zenith is a tailor.

Sophie Aaren is a florist who notices angry voices and commotion nearby, wonders what is happening, and says that everything has seemed strange lately. Her lines show her awareness is limited to what she hears and observes.
George Goodman runs a general goods shop and also supplies ammunition. His established role is practical and commercial.
Brandon Eiredeck identifies himself as a delivery man, pleading that he is only doing his job. He cowers, conveying fear.
Brock Thriss is Stratholme’s blacksmith, offering goods and quick repairs. He works amid the city’s present commotion, serving visitors who need equipment maintained or replaced.
Robert Pierce sells ammunition from his stall in Stratholme while the city is in turmoil.

Leeka Turner sells shields and offers repairs, but refuses to sell maces while Stratholme’s streets are unsettled; she fears one of her weapons could injure an innocent. She hopes visitors are not preparing for a fight and worries about the angry crowds outside.

Patricia O’Reilly is Magistrate Barthilas’s assistant, trying to calm Stratholme’s people while he is busy or unavailable. She urges residents to return home and remain calm, and asks visitors not to go back or disturb the magistrate.
Mechanical Greeter RY7R is the mechanical greeter for Fras Siabi’s Premium Tobacco. Its programmed message says that Siabi is away and invites visitors to return tomorrow, ending with a beep.

An agitated Stratholme citizen joins the crowd’s angry demands for leadership, calling for Magistrate Barthilas to come out. The citizen also blames sickness in the household on tainted food, including grain and poison bought from local sellers.

Agitated Stratholme Residents are townspeople whose shouted pleas show confusion and alarm: they ask for Barthilas and the magistrate, demand leadership, wonder what to do, and press to be let through.

place_records.text: You are in The Culling of Stratholme, a city of the past reached through the Caverns of Time in Tanaris. Undead forces hold it under Meathook and Mal'ganis, the greatest of its masters. Risen zombies and ghouls fill the place, and the infected people here are at risk of becoming Mal'ganis's undead slaves. Suspicious grain may carry the plague, and the Infinite Dragonflight is still working to deceive Prince Arthas of Lordaeron about it.
